audit.why: Poppy 56.97% over 330 games — a strong lane. EVEN 6/10 understates it slightly but the shape is right: Poppy owns 2 through first item, Swain reclaims it soul-stacked.

audit.whatIsWrong: Row 6 said Poppy while whys[6] and spikes[3] both say Swain reclaims the game; row 4 said Skill while whys[4] says 'you win the extended all-in'. Both also disagree with the packet chart.
audit.corrected: Row 4 to Poppy, row 6 to Swain, both layers, one group, with the 2+ items rating and why brought in line. Row 3 left on Skill — its why genuinely reads even.

audit.whatIsWrong: Two errors. (1) 'W deletes his dash' — Swain has no dash anywhere in his kit. (2) The page claimed in three places that Poppy's R interrupts Swain's 'R drain channel'. Demonic Ascension is a transformation with no channel — Riot's text says the form is indefinite as long as he keeps draining champions, and the kit carries no channel flag. CC does not cancel it.
audit.why: Telling a player their ultimate cancels Swain's ult is the kind of claim that loses the fight it was spent on. What Keeper's Verdict actually does is knock him out of the 650-range drain radius, which is still the right play.
audit.corrected: R restated as punting him out of the drain radius or off a Nevermove root; Nevermove named as the E root-then-pull with its 12s cooldown; W restated as the armour/MR steroid.

audit.whatIsWrong: Anti-heal was listed in itemization but never tied to a moment.
audit.why: Flagged missing interaction: Ravenous Flock heals off every Soul Fragment and permanently raises his max health, so Grievous Wounds timing decides every extended trade — especially after 6.
audit.corrected: Written into the late paragraph as a precondition for fighting him.

audit.whatIsWrong: The tracked cooldown was Demonic Ascension (120s), which is not what decides lane trades.
audit.why: Nevermove at 12/11.5/11/10.5/10s is his only lockdown; sidestep it and the all-in is free.
audit.corrected: Cooldown lines re-pointed at Nevermove with the real number, Ascension kept for the level-6 note.

edits.before: Swain at level 1-2 is a slow, immobile drain-mage with no escape, which is exactly what you eat. His only lockdown is E (a slow projectile pull) into W bomb — sidestep the E and he has nothing. Once you hit 2-3, walk up behind your own wall, E him into it for the stun and slam Q for the max-HP chunk; his flat Q poke can't trade with that. Don't facetank his W landing zone while it ticks, and don't all-in while his E is up.
edits.after: Swain at level 1-2 is a slow, immobile drain-mage with no escape, which is exactly what you eat. His only lockdown is Nevermove (E, 12s) — a slow wave that roots on the way back and then lets him pull you in. Sidestep it and he has nothing. From 2-3, walk up behind your own wall, E him into it for the stun and slam Q for the max-HP chunk; Death's Hand can't trade with that. Don't stand in Vision of Empire, and never all-in while his E is up.

edits.before: Levels 4-6 are yours. He's grounded and slow, so your E gap-close is unconditional and your W steroid lets you tank his Q+W poke through the all-in. At 6, his R is a sustained drain channel he wants to facetank you with — your R tap-knockup interrupts it or peels you off his E-root, and you win the extended trade his low burst can't close. Bait the E pull, dodge it, then commit.
edits.after: Levels 4-6 are yours. He is slow and escape-less, so your E gap-close is unconditional and the W steroid tanks his Death's Hand poke through the all-in. At 6 he transforms and drains everyone near him — CC does not cancel the form, so use R to punt him out of the 650-range drain instead, or off a Nevermove root. Bait the E, sidestep it, then commit on its 12s.

edits.before: This is where Swain takes the lane back. Soul-stacked, full-AP, his R becomes a permanent AOE lifesteal aura and his E pull-root locks you from range before you ever reach him. Your flat percent-HP Q doesn't scale into that, and W only denies dashes — he has none to deny. Close the game on your early lead; if it goes long, you're a peel-frontline who flanks the backline, not the one killing Swain.
edits.after: This is where Swain takes the lane back. Soul-stacked and full AP, his R is a permanent drain aura and Nevermove roots you from range before you ever reach him. Ravenous Flock heals him off every fragment, so Grievous Wounds has to be on him before any extended fight; your flat Q does not scale into that. Close the game on your early lead — if it goes long you're a peel-frontline who flanks, not the one killing Swain.

notes: Biggest fix: the page claimed three times that Poppy's R interrupts Demonic Ascension. Swain's ult is a transformation, not a channel — no channel flag in the kit, and Riot's text describes the form as indefinite while he drains. Replaced with the displacement out of the 650-range drain, which is the real play. The 'resistances-invalidated' flag on Ravenous Flock was NOT written to the page: the passive grants him max health, which does not actually invalidate the user's own MR against an AP Swain, and the existing Build-MR advice is correct. Packet defect 'never names any of Swain's abilities' is now addressed — Nevermove, Death's Hand, Vision of Empire, Ravenous Flock and Demonic Ascension all appear.
